name: FORM GSTR-3B — summary return of outward and inward supplies, input tax credit and tax paid
legal_reference: Section 39(1) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act: every registered person other than an Input Service Distributor, a non-resident taxable person and a person paying tax under section 10, 51 or 52 furnishes a return of inward and outward supplies, input tax credit, tax payable and tax paid for every calendar month or part of it — the proviso lets the Government notify a class of registered persons who furnish it for every quarter. Rule 61(1) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Rules makes that return FORM GSTR-3B, furnished electronically through the common portal, for each month under clause (i) and for each quarter under clause (ii) for the class the proviso reaches: the Quarterly Return Monthly Payment scheme, open to a registered person whose aggregate turnover did not exceed five crore rupees in the preceding financial year, who pays the tax of each of the first two months of the quarter in FORM GST PMT-06 by the twenty-fifth day of the following month under rule 61(3). So the form is filed on two cadences, the monthly one is what the statute gives everybody who has not opted in, and that is `period_default`. The statement of outward supplies, FORM GSTR-1 of section 37 and rule 59, is a separate filing invoice by invoice, which this pack does not carry; the README says what it leaves out.

deadline.legal_reference: Rule 61(1)(i) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Rules: FORM GSTR-3B for each month is furnished “on or before the twentieth day of the month succeeding such month”. A quarterly filer under rule 61(1)(ii) files on the twenty-second or the twenty-fourth day of the month after the quarter, according to the State of its principal place of business, which the Table of that clause lists — a second deadline this field cannot hold beside the first, and the README records it. Section 39(7) makes the tax due by the same last date as the return.

boxes.name: Net GST payable for the period, before the order of set-off of section 49(5)
boxes.legal_reference: Not a line of the form. Section 49(5) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act orders how the credit of Table 4(C) pays the liability of Table 6.1 — integrated tax credit first against integrated tax and then against central and State tax; central tax credit against central and then integrated tax; State tax credit against State and then integrated tax; central credit never against State tax, nor State credit against central tax — and section 49(4) with section 2(82) keeps the reverse-charge tax out of reach of the credit ledger. The common portal works that order out itself, head by head, in Table 6.1. This total is the same arithmetic without the order: all heads of 6.1 less all heads of 4(C), which is what the period settles to when no head is short of credit; where one head is, the portal asks for cash on that head and carries credit forward on another, and this figure understates the cash. Floored at zero; the opposite case is NETCRED.
